title: Sigma-table aligned rho v15s: escape act charged at the measured fire rate, Montgomery-batched inversions, bounded candidate pairs, production-load stress census, zero SIMD by -mgeneral-regs-only, total peak bytes

claims.statement: Analytic secp256k1 ECDLP claim at success >= 0.39, priced as a CONSERVATIVE PATH UPPER BOUND at the protected C=1000, in 10^3-instruction units. STEP COMPOSITION, every span recounted under ONE convention (an instruction is any line whose first token is an opcode with or without operands, so the operand-free `ret` counts; _v15r_reset_hist is 16, not 15): 744 point + 433 alignment + 604 label + 79 detector + 9 action = 1869 Ir per step, plus the escape act and the history reset on their own amortized rows at the census-MEASURED fire rate 3515/276296: escape 159256 Ir/fire x rate = 2026.033 Ir/step and reset_hist 16 Ir x rate = 0.204 Ir/step, so the DELIVERED step is 5486.62 Ir (the escape act is charged, not declared). ZERO SIMD is a compiler guarantee: the counted TU is rebuilt with -mgeneral-regs-only (NEON register file unavailable, so no q/d/v/s/h/b register can be allocated and no ASIMD-only instruction emitted) and the register-class scan of the shipped listing returns 0 matches; the mandatorily rebuilt listing also removes the two q-register stores and the movi.2d that v15r's flag-only claim left in place. BATCHED INVERSIONS are scheduled and priced: Montgomery's trick turns a batch of n affine additions into 1 inversion + 3(n-1) modmuls, with the batch size equal to the adds per call (walk refill 67 steps, init_for_Q 2062 adds, escape 66 adds), so every add is charged its flat 744 Ir plus its amortized inversion share (713.2 / 1582.4 / 1596.0 Ir per add) and no add is priced at a batch it does not belong to. The jump table is rebuilt PER CHALLENGE by the shipped v15r_init_for_Q (J_k = [u_k]P0 + [v_k]Q, v_k = 1 + k mod 15), charged in full as its own one-time row per challenge plus a one-time static-table row; the fixed-Q0 build is kept as a control and recovers 0/8. The detector's counters BRANCH: v15r_action trips at rep >= 16 or win >= 67 and invokes the shipped v15r_escape (fresh coins as a random 16-bit label offset plus the matching point action and a full history reset); a forced 120-walk test records 210 trips, 210 verified state resets and 210 endpoint holds after reset, while the detached-action control records 5802 trips and 0 resets. The endpoint comparison is DERIVED from scripts/invariant-row.json (P == [a]G + [c]Q): 0/96 violations on 24 x 200 shipped steps, and the v15q hand-written side fails 2/2 as a planted control. RECOVERY IS BOUNDED: a walker halts at the first collision it reports (v15o_report copies the resident's label pair out AT THE MATCHING WRITE, before any eviction) and makes exactly one solve attempt, so delivered candidate pairs <= workers = 2^20 and solve attempts <= 2^20, each priced at 61788 Ir (1 inversion + 4 modmuls) and verified at 361216 Ir -- no unbounded candidate stream and no retry loop. POOL AND PRODUCTION LOAD: slot = hash(x) mod 2^34 per shard, four probes, evict-oldest, 2^34 x 96 B per shard, 2^28 shards, 2^62 resident records. The production per-shard load is PRINTED, not assumed: (reports/shards)/slots_per_shard = (2^126.453 / 2^28) / 2^34 = 2^64.453 writes per slot, i.e. SATURATED. The law the algorithm actually reads is occupancy plus match capture, both of which survive saturation: a report meets the RESIDENT records at its own write and the matching pair is copied out at that instant, so historical survival of old records is not a precondition. Measured basis: the census's production_load_stress arms run the shipped object with every arrival writing into a small pool, reaching 0.50, 0.99, 2.00, 4.23, 10.30 writes per slot (vs 0.5 in the retention curve) and retention-as-history collapsed, with success 43/43/43/43/39 of 48 per arm against the 0.39 floor; the retention curve itself is now measured out to load 8 (0.0082 at load 8). Allocation is demand-based (a shard is materialised only when a record maps to it), allocated bytes <= 442721857769029238784, and the pool is charged at its declared 442721857769029238784-byte capacity. The census runs the shipped object at the ledger-normalized budget with ONE budget column for every trial (all 256 trials and all 48 stress trials at the same S; assert max executed steps <= S): S/sqrt(N6) = 1.677048 fixture vs 1.676590 ledger (rel. 5.5e-4), 234/256 successes and a one-sided Clopper-Pearson 95% lower limit of 0.879561 on the measured 2-run fraction. The ledger charges mu = 2.842 (the inherited 1.107 is dead); this round's census re-measures 1.020, so the work bound is on the conservative side. PEAK STORAGE is one row over the whole machine: workers x sizeof(worker_t) (264 B, machine-derived and static-asserted: rec_t 88 + coefficients 64 + detector history 64 + minx 32 + counters 16) + the batch-inversion prefix scratch (67 x 64 B = 4288 B per worker) + the 442721857769029238784-byte record pool + 16 B per shard of metadata + jump table + code + advice = 442721857778098634752 bytes. Exact-rational rows sum to W_time = 2^129.925309 with a planted +1 control rejected and every manifest literal regenerated from the certificate (a planted stale 430 is rejected). The claim does NOT establish a production-scale success floor beyond the measured regime: the census and its stress arms are fixture-scope, and this is a priced HOLD.
